text:
**About 200-400 W of solar panels, depending on how fast you want it to recharge.** Panels rarely deliver their rated watts, so most guides plan on about 70-75% of the label rating.

**Formula:** panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75) ([power-runtime guide](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/))

| Panel size | Daily output (4.5 sun hours, 70%) | Time to refill 1,000 Wh from empty |
|---|---|---|
| 100 W | ~315 Wh | ~3 days |
| 200 W | ~630 Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 400 W | ~1,260 Wh | Under a day |

*Source: [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)*

- **Full recharge in one day:** about 340 W at 4 peak sun hours, 270 W at 5, and 230 W at 6 ([power-runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)). Another guide estimates roughly 300 W in summer but 700 W or more in a northern winter ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Rule of thumb:** divide the battery's Wh by 5, so 200 W recharges 1,000 Wh in about a day and a half of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Sun hours:** peak sun hours are not daylight hours. Most of the US gets about 3-6 a day, and winter and cloudy regions are at the low end ([power-runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).

**Before you buy panels, check your station's specs:**
1. **Maximum solar input watts.** Mid-range 1,000-1,500 Wh stations typically accept 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W, and panels above the cap add nothing ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
2. **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside it. Going over can damage the charge controller, and panels wired in series add their voltages ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
3. **Connector type.** Panels usually use MC4 connectors, while stations take XT60, DC barrel, or proprietary ports, so you may need an adapter.

Running appliances from the station while it charges slows the net recharge, since net charge is solar input minus load.
